gap_description.definition: Main plots show continuous time axes with regularly spaced ticks (e.g., 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 or similar depending on subplot) and no abrupt numerical jumps; the small inset panels are separate, zoomed plots (early time points), not continuations of the main x-axis.
Y-axis is normalized intensity (0–1) with continuous labeling; there is no skipped range or sudden jump in tick labels.

justify_why_gaps_are_missing.justification: The x-axis tick spacing and numeric sequence are regular and continuous in each main plot. The inset is an independent, separate axis (zoom of early times) rather than a compressed continuation of the main axis, so no axis-break marker is required.
Y-axis values are shown on a continuous normalized scale (0–1) with no skipped values or spacing anomalies that would indicate a hidden gap.
